newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. postpones action on anti-EU meat sanctions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. postpones action on anti-EU meat sanctions.

text.p: The United States has postponed to April 30 any anti-EU action to step up inspections of EU meat imports to allow transatlantic talks on veterinary standards to continue, a European Commission spokesman said on Tuesday.
"The Americans have called off any action until April 30 to allow talks to continue," the spokesman told Reuters.
U.S. and EU officials ended face-to-face talks last Friday after failing to reach an agreement over meat import inspection regulations.
The complicated talks have covered a wide range of issues and sectors -- including the beef and pork industry, the poultry industry, the pet food sector, and the dairy and egg sectors.

U.S. industry sources anticipated late on Monday that Washington would avert a potentially nasty trade war with the European Union by agreeing to accept a deal in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks on everything except poultry.
Washington had set a Tuesday deadline for a deal to be reached and threatened to remove more than 100 European meat and poultry plants from its approved exporters list if no deal came.
